result:
I added a basic registry of 4N articles, modelled on the existing `Grant` feature. I didn't run the migration or any tests, so none of it has been exercised. I only checked that the model file has valid Ruby syntax.

The issue gives no requirements beyond its title, so I kept to what the codebase already supports. A `FourNArticle` record holds a title, journal, publication year, DOI, a justification and the professor it belongs to. It's managed through an ActiveScaffold screen, "Artigos 4N", in the professors menu, with changes tracked by paper_trail. A professor can only create articles for themselves and edit their own; other roles follow the same permission setup as `Grant`.

The files are in `app/` (model, controller, helper), `config/` (routes, navigation, pt-BR locale), `db/` (migration and `schema.rb`) and `spec/factories`.

None of the rules from the issue's open questions are implemented:
- the 4 × N limit
- quadrennium eligibility
- de-duplicating articles with several professor authors
- consolidation
- export

The only validations are required fields, a positive publication year, and no duplicate title for the same professor and year. The issue itself asks for answers on those rules first. I also didn't add specs.

The migration is `db/migrate/20241203180000_create_four_n_articles.rb`. I edited `db/schema.rb` by hand to match, so it's worth running `rails db:migrate` and checking the schema diff.
